rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sending of Muhammad has exceptional rank and distinction among prophetic missions.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الإرسال أرسلناك ، يعني : أرسلناك إرسالا له شأن وفضل على سائر الإرسالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent among the last community, after many earlier nations, and is the final prophet.
rows.anchor: فى أمة قد تقدمتها أمم كثيرة فهي آخر الأمم وأنت خاتم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His task is to recite to them the magnificent revealed Book.
rows.anchor: لتقرأ عليهم الكتاب العظيم الذي أوحينا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people reject the All-Merciful, whose mercy encompasses everything and from whom all their blessings come.
rows.anchor: بالبليغ الرحمة الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء ، وما بهم من نعمة فمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their unbelief rejects the favor of Muhammad's mission and the miraculous Qur'an, which confirms earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: فكفروا بنعمته في إرسال مثلك إليهم وإنزال هذا القرآن المعجز المصدق لسائر الكتب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one Lord, exalted above partners.
rows.anchor: قل هو ربى } الواحد المتعالي عن الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad relies on God for support against his opponents and returns to Him for reward for enduring and striving against them.
rows.anchor: عليه توكلت } في نصرتي عليكم { وإليه متاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the city are the people of Sodom, whose judge was proverbial for injustice; they welcomed the angels eagerly.
rows.anchor: أهل سدوم التي ضرب بقاضيها المثل في الجور ، مستبشرين بالملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot asks that his guests not be disgraced: mistreating a guest or neighbor harms the host, while honoring an associate honors him.
rows.anchor: لأن من أسيء إلى ضيفه أو جاره فقد أسيء إليه ، كما أن من أكرم من يتصل به فقد أكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea not to humiliate Lot can mean not degrading him, or not shaming him in the sense of modest embarrassment.
rows.anchor: ولا تذلون بإذلال ضيفي ، من الخزي وهو الهوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From the world” can mean that Lot should not shelter, repel attackers from, or interpose himself between the townspeople and their targets.
rows.anchor: عن أن تجير منهم أحدا ، أو تدفع عنهم ، أو تمنع بيننا وبينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople attacked anyone, while Lot restrained them from wrongdoing; they threatened to expel him if he persisted.
rows.anchor: يتعرضون لكل أحد ، وكان يقوم صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the townspeople objected to Lot hosting and lodging visitors at all.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عن ضيافة الناس وإنزالهم ، وكانوا نهوه أن يضيف أحدا قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My daughters” refers to women generally: each community's men and women are called the sons and daughters of its prophet; Lot offers them in marriage so the guests are left alone.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى النساء ؛ لأن كل أمة أولاد نبيها رجالهم بنوه ونساؤهم بناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's conditional appeal signals doubt that the men will accept his proposal.
rows.anchor: شك في قبولهم لقوله ، كأنه قال : إن فعلتم ما أقول لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Lot means that they should satisfy desire lawfully through women rather than unlawfully through his guests.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن كنتم تريدون قضاء الشهوة فيما أحل الله دون ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one construction, the angels address Lot with the oath “by your life,” saying the people are lost in their frenzy.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول ، أي قالت الملائكة للوط عليه السلام : لعمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God addresses the Messenger and swears by his life, a distinction granted to him alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وأنه أقسم بحياته وما أقسم بحياة أحد قط كرامة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms of “life” mean the same; the oath uses the lighter open vowel because people swear frequently, and omits its predicate as in “by God.”
rows.anchor: والعمر والعمر واحد ، إلا أنهم خصوا القسم بالمفتوح لإيثار الأخف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are so deluded that their reason and ability to distinguish their error from sound advice have disappeared, so they cannot heed Lot.
rows.anchor: أي غوايتهم التي أذهبت عقولهم وتمييزهم بين الخطأ الذي هم عليه وبين الصواب الذي تشير به عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation has “in their intoxication” and another has “in their intoxications.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( في سكرهم وفي سكراتهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry that struck the people was Gabriel's cry.
rows.anchor: { الصيحة } صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “At sunrise” means entering the time when the sun rises.
rows.anchor: داخلين في الشروق وهو بزوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones of sijjīl are clay bearing an inscription, as supported by the description of marked stones from clay.
rows.anchor: قيل : من طين ، عليه كتاب من السجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discerning are perceptive observers who examine carefully until they recognize the reality marked by a thing; the verb means recognizing its sign in someone.
rows.anchor: للمتفرسين المتأملين . وحقيقة المتوسمين النظار المتثبتون في نظرهم حتى يعرفوا حقيقة سمة الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “its upper part became its lower” refers to the towns of Lot's people.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { عاليها سافلها } لقرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” means the towns' traces, which remain on a well-traveled road and are still visible.
rows.anchor: ثابت يسلكه الناس لم يندرس بعد ، وهم يبصرون تلك الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible remains warn Quraysh, as does the reminder that they pass the ruins in the morning.
rows.anchor: وهو تنبيه لقريش كقوله : { وإنكم * لتمرون عليهم مصبحين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Horses, mules, and donkeys are coordinated with livestock and were created for riding and adornment.
rows.anchor: عطف على الأنعام ، أي : وخلق هؤلاء للركوب والزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their creation for riding and adornment, with no mention of eating them after edible livestock is mentioned, is an argument for the prohibition on eating their meat.
rows.anchor: وقد احتج على حرمة أكل لحومهن بأن علل خلقها بالركوب والزينة ، ولم يذكر الأكل بعد ما ذكره في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As adornment” is a purpose-object coordinated with the syntactic position of “for you to ride them.”
rows.anchor: لأنه مفعول له ، وهو معطوف على محل لتركبوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated phrases differ grammatically because riding is the addressees' action, while adornment is the Creator's action.
rows.anchor: لأن الركوب فعل المخاطبين ، وأما الزينة ففعل الزائن وهو الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading without the conjunction means the animals were created as adornment for riding.
rows.anchor: أي : وخلقها زينة لتركبوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “adornment” is a circumstantial description: they were created to be ridden while being beautiful.
rows.anchor: أو تجعل زينة حالا منها ، أي : وخلقها لتركبوها وهي زينة وجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He creates what you do not know” may mean unknown things created for people, whose details are hidden, mentioned as blessings alongside known things and as evidence of power.
rows.anchor: ما يخلق فينا ولنا مما لا نعلم كنهه وتفاصيله ويمن علينا بذكره كما من بالأشياء المعلومة مع الدلالة على قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God informs people that unknown creatures exist, increasing the evidence of His power while concealing them for a reason; these may include unimaginable things in Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: بأن له من الخلائق ما لا علم لنا به ، ليزيدنا دلالة على اقتداره بالإخبار بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unknown creations may be creatures of Paradise and Hell beyond anyone's imagination.
rows.anchor: وقد حمل على ما خلق في الجنة والنار ، مما لم يبلغه وهم أحد ، ولا خطر على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fresh, tender flesh is fish; it is called tender because it spoils quickly and should be eaten promptly.
rows.anchor: هو السمك ، ووصفه بالطراوة ؛ لأن الفساد يسرع إليه ، فيسارع إلى أكله خيفة للفساد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths follow customary usage: unqualified “meat” ordinarily does not mean fish, so eating fish does not break an oath not to eat meat.
rows.anchor: مبنى الأيمان على العادة ، وعادة الناس إذا ذكر اللحم على الإطلاق أن لا يفهم منه السمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example is that a servant bringing fish when told to buy meat would rightly be rebuked.
rows.anchor: وإذا قال الرجل لغلامه : اشتر بهذه الدراهم لحما فجاء بالسمك ، كان حقيقا بالإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, although God calls an unbeliever an animal, riding one does not break an oath not to ride an animal.
rows.anchor: فلو حلف حالف لا يركب دابة فركب كافرا لم يحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adornments are pearls and coral; women's wearing them counts as the men's adornment because the women belong to them and beautify themselves for them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بلبسهم : لبس نسائهم ، لأنهن من جملتهم ، ولأنهن إنما يتزين بها من أجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Cleaving” is a ship cutting through water with its hull.
rows.anchor: المخر : شق الماء بحيزومها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains “cleaving” as the sound of ships running with the wind.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء : هو صوت جري الفلك بالرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's bounty means engaging in trade.
rows.anchor: وابتغاء الفضل : التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond singular and dual, nouns do not themselves specify a particular number, so number and counted noun are normally combined; singulars and duals already encode their count.
rows.anchor: وأما رجل ورجلان وفرس وفرسان ، فمعدودان فيهما دلالة على العدد ، فلا حاجة إلى أن يقال : رجل واحد ورجلان اثنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the dual already signals two, “two gods” adds an emphatic numeral to make the intended count and concern with actual oneness explicit.
rows.anchor: فإذا أريدت الدلالة على أن المعنى به منهما ، والذي يساق إليه الحديث هو العدد شفع بما يؤكده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying only “a god” would assert divinity without clearly asserting exclusive oneness.
rows.anchor: إنما هو إله ، ولم تؤكده بواحد : لم يحسن ، وخيل أنك تثبت الإلهية لا الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So fear Me” shifts from third person to first person; this rhetorical turn is possible because the speaker is the central perspective.
rows.anchor: نقل للكلام عن الغيبة إلى التكلم ، وجاز لأن الغالب هو المتكلم ، وهو من طريقة الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person shift heightens the warning compared with “fear Him” or continuing in the preceding first-person form.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ في الترهيب من قوله : وإياه فارهبوه ، ومن أن يجيء ما قبله على لفظ المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation to the bee is inspiration, inward prompting, and teaching in a manner whose mechanism no one can know.
rows.anchor: الإيحاء إلى النحل : إلهامها والقذف في قلوبها وتعليمها على وجه هو أعلم به ، لا سبيل لأحد إلى الوقوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee's craft, delicate management, and accurate pursuit of its welfare plainly show that God gave it knowledge and discernment, as He gives reason to rational beings.
rows.anchor: دلائل بينة شاهدة على أن الله أودعها علما بذلك وفطنها ، كما أولى أولي العقول عقولهم

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads “the bee” with both initial vowels open; the noun is masculine, while feminine agreement follows its meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن وثاب { إلى النحل } بفتحتين . وهو مذكر كالنحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That it take” is an explanatory particle because revelation here carries the sense of saying.
rows.anchor: هي أن المفسرة ؛ لأن الإيحاء فيه معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces the bāʾ in “houses” with kasra because of the following yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بيوتا ) بكسر الباء لأجل الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for raising structures is read with the rāʾ either kasra or ḍamma and means raising roofs.
rows.anchor: و { يعرشون } بكسر الراء وضمها : يرفعون من سقوف البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean the places people make for bees in mountains, trees, and houses where honey forms; the pronoun refers to people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما يبنون للنحل في الجبال والشجر والبيوت من الأماكن التي تتعسل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “from” means some of each kind: bees do not make homes in every mountain, tree, or built place.
rows.anchor: أريد معنى البعضية ، وأن لا تبني بيوتها في كل جبل وكل شجر وكل ما يعرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All fruits” covers the fruits bees visit and habitually eat: first they make homes, then eat whatever fruit they desire.
rows.anchor: إحاطة بالثمرات التي تجرسها النحل وتعتاد أكلها ، أي ابني البيوت ، ثم كلي من كل ثمرة تشتهينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee's Lord-guided paths may be the routes He inspires and teaches it for making honey.
rows.anchor: أي الطرق التي ألهمك وأفهمك في عمل العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the paths are the channels through which God transforms what the bee eats into bitter-light honey in its body.
rows.anchor: أو فاسلكي ما أكلت في سبل ربك ، أي في مسالكه التي يحيل فيها بقدرته النور المر عسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the paths are the bee's return routes to its hive from distant flowers, made easy so it neither struggles nor loses its way.
rows.anchor: أو إذا أكلت الثمار في المواضع البعيدة من بيوتك ، فاسلكي إلى بيوتك راجعة سبل ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author has heard that bees sometimes travel to distant regions to forage when nearby areas suffer drought.
rows.anchor: فقد بلغني أنها ربما أجدب عليها ما حولها فتسافر إلى البلد البعيد في طلب النجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading of the command is to set out to eat fruits by following the routes where they are found.
rows.anchor: ثم اقصدي أكل الثمرات فاسلكلي في طلبها في مظانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Gentle” can describe the paths: God has subdued, prepared, and smoothed them for the bee, as He made the earth tractable for people.
rows.anchor: جمع ذلول ، وهي حال من السبل ؛ لأن الله ذللها لها ووطأها وسهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “gentle” describes the bee itself as compliant with the command and unresisting.
rows.anchor: أي : وأنت ذلل منقادة لما أمرت به غير ممتنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink that emerges from the bees is honey, described as a drink because it is consumed that way.
rows.anchor: يريد العسل ، لأنه مما يشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey comes in white, black, yellow, and red varieties.
rows.anchor: منه أبيض وأسود وأصفر وأحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey is one of the familiar beneficial remedies, but the verse does not claim that it cures every patient, just as no medicine cures everyone.
rows.anchor: وليس الغرض أنه شفاء لكل مريض ، كما أن كل دواء كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form of “healing” may magnify the healing in honey or mean that it contains some healing; both readings are possible.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره إما لتعظيم الشفاء الذي فيه ، أو لأن فيه بعض الشفاء ، وكلاهما محتمل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man says his brother has a stomach complaint; the Prophet repeatedly tells him to give honey, explaining that God's word is true while the brother's stomach is wrong, and the man recovers after another dose.
rows.anchor: ( 587 ) أن رجلا جاء إليه فقال : إن أخي يشتكي بطنه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says honey cures every disease and the Qur'an cures what is in the hearts, so people should use both cures.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود : ( 588 ) العسل شفاء من كل داء ، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls it a heretical Rāfiḍī interpretation to take the bees as ʿAlī and his followers.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التأويلات الرافضة : أن المراد بالنحل علي وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also ridicules an interpretation told to the Mahdī that the bees are Banū Hāshim and the honey from their bodies is knowledge; a retort and the caliphs' laughter made it a joke.
rows.anchor: إنما النحل بنو هاشم ، يخرج من بطونهم العلم ، فقال له رجل : جعل الله طعامك وشرابك مما يخرج من بطونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In ignorance” is circumstantial: the sinners acted without knowing God and His punishment, or without considering the outcome because desire overwhelmed them.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال ، أي : عملوا السوء جاهلين غير عارفين بالله وبعقابه ، أو غير متدبرين للعاقبة لغلبة الشهوة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After it” means after repentance.
rows.anchor: من بعدها } من بعد التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes “the All-Merciful” genitive as an adjective of the one who created; the nominative is preferable, either as praise or as a subject pointing back to the Creator.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( الرحمان ) مجرورا صفة لمن خلق والرفع أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “the All-Merciful” is genitive, the clause “established Himself over the Throne” is the predicate of an omitted subject; with nominative praise it can be that or a second predicate.
rows.anchor: قلت : إذا جررت فهي خبر مبتدأ محذوف لا غير وإن رفعت جاز أن تكون كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing oneself on a throne conventionally signifies kingship, whether or not the ruler literally sits on a throne; the expression is vivid and explanatory.
rows.anchor: جعلوه كناية عن الملك فقالوا : استوى فلان على العرش يريدون ملك وإن لم يقعد على السرير البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, an open or tied hand conventionally means generosity or stinginess without imagining a literal hand or its binding.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قولك : يد فلان مبسوطة ، ويد فلان مغلولة ، بمعنى أنه جواد أو بخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the hand as bounty and then forcing the dual form is strained and departs from rhetorical understanding.
rows.anchor: والتفسير بالنعمة والتمحل للتثنية من ضيق الطعن والمسافرة عن علم البيان مسيرة أعوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is beneath the soil” means beneath the seven earths.
rows.anchor: { وما تحت الثرى } تحت سبع الأرضين

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb identifies what lies beneath the soil as the rock under the seventh earth.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب وعن السدي : هو الصخرة التي تحت الأرض السابعة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī likewise identifies what lies beneath the soil as the rock under the seventh earth.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب وعن السدي : هو الصخرة التي تحت الأرض السابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks both prophets but directs the challenge to Moses because Moses is the principal prophet and Aaron his minister and follower.
rows.anchor: خاطب الاثنين ، ووجه النداء إلى أحدهما وهو موسى ؛ لأنه الأصل في النبوة ، وهارون وزيره وتابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh's malice made him demand Moses' speech, knowing Aaron's eloquence and Moses' speech impediment.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يحمله خبثه ودعارته على استدعاء كلام موسى دون كلام أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “His creation” may be the first object of “gave”: God gave each creature everything it needs and can use.
rows.anchor: أول مفعولي أعطى ، أي : أعطى خليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the second object: God gave every thing a form suited to its function, as the eye, ear, nose, limbs, and tongue suit their uses.
rows.anchor: أو ثانيهما ، أي : أعطى كل شيء صورته وشكله الذي يطابق المنفعة المنوطة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God gave each animal a matching counterpart of its own kind, including male and female pairs among livestock and people.
rows.anchor: والبعير والناقة ، والرجل والمرأة ، فلم يزاوج منها شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading treats “His creation” as an adjective of either adjoining noun, meaning that God did not withhold His gift and favor from anything He created.
rows.anchor: أي : كل شيء خلقه الله لم يخله من عطائه وإنعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then He guided” means that God taught each creature how to benefit from what it was given and how to obtain it.
rows.anchor: أي عرف كيف يرتفق بما أعطى ، وكيف يتوصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author praises Moses' answer as concise, comprehensive, and clear to a fair-minded person seeking truth.
rows.anchor: ولله در هذا الجواب ما أخصره وما أجمعه ، وما أبينه لمن ألقى الذهن ونظر بعين الإنصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks about the condition of earlier generations, including which were wretched and which were happy; Moses says this belongs to the unseen known only to God.
rows.anchor: سأله عن حال من تقدم وخلا من القرون ، وعن شقاء من شقي منهم وسعادة من سعد ، فأجابه بأن هذا سؤال عن الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he knows only what the Knower of the unseen has revealed; the generations' histories are recorded with God in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وما أنا إلا عبد مثلك لا أعلم منه إلا ما أخبرني به علام الغيوب ، وعلم أحوال القرون مكتوب عند الله في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot err or forget.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز على الله أن يخطيء شيئا أو ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “miss” can mean failing to find something in its place, like losing a road or home.
rows.anchor: يقال : ضللت الشيء إذا أخطأته في مكانه فلم تهتد له ، كقولك : ضللت الطريق والمنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with the causative form means that God does not lose or neglect anything.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( يضل ) من أضله إذا ضيعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God does not leave an unbeliever without punishment or a monotheist without recompense.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه ، ولا يترك من وحده حتى يجازيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh may be challenging whether God can encompass the countless, dispersed details of all past generations; Moses answers that all beings are encompassed by God's knowledge and recorded, beyond human error and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون فرعون قد نازعه في إحاطة الله بكل شيء وتبينه لكل معلوم ، فتعنت ، وقال : ما تقول في سوالف القرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who made” can be an adjective of “my Lord,” a predicate of an omitted subject, or an accusative phrase of praise.
rows.anchor: مرفوع صفة لربي . أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو منصوب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan reading “a bed” treats the earth as spread like a child's bed, or as something its inhabitants spread out.
rows.anchor: { مهادا } قراءة أهل الكوفة ، أي : مهدها مهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He made paths through it” means that God placed routes amid mountains, valleys, and plains.
rows.anchor: أي حصل لكم فيها سبلا ووسطها بين الجبال والأودية والبراري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in “then We brought forth” from third-person to first-person marks God's sovereign command over varied things and signals that no one else can produce them.
rows.anchor: { فأخرجنا } انتقل فيه من لفظ الغيبة إي لفظ المتكلم المطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinds are called pairs because they are coupled or associated with one another.
rows.anchor: أصنافا ، سميت بذلك لأنها مزدوجة ومقترنة بعضها مع بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Varied” may modify the kinds or the vegetation; the varieties differ in usefulness, taste, color, scent, and form, with some suited to people and some to animals.
rows.anchor: يعني أنها شتى مختلفة النفع والطعم واللون والرائحة والشكل ، بعضها يصلح للناس وبعضها للبهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides livestock with fodder left over from human needs, which people themselves cannot eat.
rows.anchor: من نعمته عز وعلا أن أرزاق العباد إنما تحصل بعمل الأنعام . وقد جعل الله علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Eat and pasture” describes God's bringing forth vegetation with permission to eat some and feed some to livestock.
rows.anchor: المعنى : أخرجنا أصناف النبات آذنين في الانتفاع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the Children of Israel recalls their rescue from the sea and Pharaoh's destruction; although it may address Israelites in Muhammad's time, the author prefers the earlier audience.
rows.anchor: خطاب لهم بعد إنجائهم من البحر وإهلاك آل فرعون ، وقيل : هو للذين كانوا منهم في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier address means “We said, O Children of Israel”; omission of “We said” is common in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والوجه هو الأول ، أي : قلنا يا بني إسرائيل ، وحذف القول كثير في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses first-person forms from “We saved you” through “We provided you,” retaining the language of promise and covenant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( أنجيتكم ) إلى ( رزقتكم ) ، وعلى لفظ الوعد والمواعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts “the faith” in the genitive by attraction to a nearby word, like the phrase “a lizard's hole, broken.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء { الايمان } بالجر على الجوار ، نحو ( جحر ضب خرب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls Israel's rescue, the destruction of its enemy, Moses' appointed private audience at the mountain, the Torah on tablets, and other blessings.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم النعمة في نجاتهم وهلاك عدوهم ، وفيما واعد موسى صلوات الله عليه من المناجاة بجانب الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is addressed to Israel because it concerned them through their prophet and leaders, and its benefits established their religion and law.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدى المواعدة إليهم لأنها لابستهم واتصلت بهم حيث كانت لنبيهم ونقبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exceeding the limits of blessings includes denying them, being distracted from gratitude by pleasure, spending on sins, denying the poor their due, extravagance, arrogance, and pride.
rows.anchor: أن يتعدوا حدود الله فيها بأن يكفروها ويشغلهم اللهو والتنعم عن القيام بشكرها ، وأن ينفقوها في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “so it descends,” while ʿAbd Allāh reads “do not let it descend.”
rows.anchor: قرىء { فيحل } وعن عبد الله ( لا يحلن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, “becomes due” means obligation, as a debt comes due; with ḍamma, it means descending. God's anger is described as descending because it is punishment.
rows.anchor: { ومن يحلل } المكسور في معنى الوجوب ، من حل الدين يحل إذا وجب أداؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He fell” means he perished, originally by falling from a mountain and dying, or by an irrecoverable fall.
rows.anchor: { هوى } هلك . وأصله أن يسقط من جبل فيهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arabic poem illustrates the sense of falling from a mountain and being crushed.
rows.anchor: قالت : هوى من رأس مرقبة … ففتت تحتها كبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance here is steadfastness in the previously named guidance of repentance, faith, and righteous action.
rows.anchor: الاهتداء : هو الاستقامة والثبات على الهدى المذكور وهو التوبة والإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then” marks a difference of rank as well as sequence: remaining upright in goodness is higher and better than goodness itself.
rows.anchor: وكلمة التراخي دلت على تباين المنزلتين دلالتها على تباين الوقتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question reproaches Moses for hurrying away from the others; he had gone with the leaders for the appointed meeting, then advanced out of longing to speak with God and fulfill the promise, thinking this would please God more.
rows.anchor: أي شيء عجل بك عنهم على سبيل الإنكار ، وكان قد مضى مع النقباء إلى الطور على الموعد المضروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses overlooked that God times actions according to wisdom and the interests specific to each time.
rows.anchor: وزل عنه أنه عز وجل ما وقت أفعاله إلا نظرا إلى دواعي الحكمة ، وعلما بالمصالح المتعلقة بكل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The people” means the tribal leaders who accompanied Moses.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالقوم : النقباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that Moses had left the whole people before the appointed time has no sound basis and conflicts with his saying that they are close behind him.
rows.anchor: وليس لقول من جوز أن يراد جميع قومه وأن يكون قد فارقهم قبل الميعاد وجه صحيح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the word for “my track” with kasra on its initial hamza.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو ويعقوب ( إثري ) بالكسر

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads it with ḍamma; he also has a shortened reading “ula.”
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر ( أثري ) بالضم . وعنه أيضا : ( أولى ) بالقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ithra” is more eloquent than “athar”; the latter is attested for a sword's sheen and in textual originals but is unusual.
rows.anchor: والإثر أفصح من الأثر . وأما الأثر فمسموع في فرند السيف مدون في الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the question asks why Moses hurried, his reply first addresses its reproach by saying he only went a little ahead; he then explains that he hurried to please God.
rows.anchor: فكان أهم الأمرين إلى موسى بسط العذر وتمهيد العلة في نفس ما أنكر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses excuses himself by saying that he advanced only a short, customary distance, as the leader of a delegation may do.
rows.anchor: فكان أهم الأمرين إلى موسى بسط العذر وتمهيد العلة في نفس ما أنكر عليه ، فاعتل بأنه لم يوجد مني إلا تقدم يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then answers the question about motive: he hurried to God so that God would be pleased.
rows.anchor: ثم عقبه بجواب السؤال عن السبب فقال : { وعجلت إليك رب لترضى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, awe at God's reproach overwhelmed Moses and distracted him from giving the logically ordered answer.
rows.anchor: حار لما ورد عليه من التهيب لعتاب الله
